text: Patient: Robert Johnson is a 67-year-old male who presents to the clinic with chest pain. He reports the pain started three days ago and is worse with exertion. Past medical history includes hypertension and high cholesterol. His date of birth is 03/15/1957. MRN: 482913. He can be reached at (555) 234-5678 or by email at robert.johnson@example.com. Home address: 1234 Maple Street, Springfield, IL 62701. SSN: 123-45-6789. Account No: 88421033. Vitals today: BP 142/88, HR 78, Temp 98.6F, O2 sat 98% on room air. Labs from last week show LDL 160 and A1c 6.1. Exam reveals regular heart rhythm with no murmurs and clear lungs. Dr. Emily Chen evaluated the patient and ordered an ECG, which showed normal sinus rhythm. Plan: start low-dose aspirin and atorvastatin, schedule a stress test within two weeks, and follow up in clinic in one month. The patient was advised to seek emergency care if pain worsens.

Maria Garcia is a 94-year-old female seen for diabetes follow-up. She was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes in 2019. DOB: March 5, 1932. MRN: 771204. Contact phone: 555-876-1234. She lives at 78 Oak Avenue, Riverside, CA 92501. Recent A1c is 8.2, up from 7.4 six months ago. She reports increased thirst and frequent urination over the past month. Current medications include metformin 1000 mg twice daily. Vitals: BP 138/82, HR 72, weight 168 lbs. Exam shows no foot ulcers and intact pedal pulses. Mr. James Carter, her son, attended the visit and will help with medication reminders. Plan: add a DPP-4 inhibitor to current metformin, refer to diabetes education, and recheck A1c in three months. Return sooner if blood sugars exceed 250.

David Kim is a 45-year-old male presenting with migraine headaches. Headaches began about two years ago and occur two to three times per month. DOB 11/02/1980. Email: david.kim@example.com. Phone: (555) 345-8890. Address: 9 Birch Lane, Madison, WI 53703. MRN: DK-883412. SSN: 987-65-4321. His father, age 88, also has a history of migraines. Neurologic exam is normal with no focal deficits. He tried ibuprofen with partial relief. Allergies: none known. Plan: start sumatriptan 50 mg as needed for acute attacks, keep a headache diary, avoid known triggers, and follow up in three months. Electronically signed by Lisa Wang, MD.
